text:
tara: Heads-up — multiple customers started escalating p95/p99 spikes over the last 45m. They all report slowed responses and retries. Main pattern: GPU workers hit OOM+severe page fault backoffs, then token p99 jumps to >2s. Logs attached below.

mike: Which pools? any common model/version?

tara: Most are on c-rw-rt/gpt-large-v2@v12 (dedicated). A subset on hosted multimodel-backend as well. Consistent repro: long chat histories with repeated system prompts -> KV cache grows and GPU memory climbs steadily (no immediate hard OOMs but fragmentation + allocator failures).

jasmin: Can you paste the allocator logs? esp failures like "cudaMalloc failed" or "out of memory on device"?

tara: Sure — snippets: 

```
[2026-03-15T10:04:02Z] WARN runtime: GPU 3 memory high: used=30.7G / 40.0G (frag=4.1G)
[2026-03-15T10:04:03Z] ERROR runtime: cudaMalloc returned out_of_memory while allocating 512MB for attention_kv_cache
[2026-03-15T10:04:03Z] WARN runtime: fallback to CPU page-fault, increased latency
[2026-03-15T10:04:05Z] INFO runtime: kv_cache_size bytes=1.9G entries=1243 growth_rate=~6.1/s
```

mike: kv_cache growth_rate looks aggressive. Are these long-prompt customers using streaming chunking that keeps appending?

tara: Yes. Pattern: chat UI keeps appending assistant messages without pruning; we've seen single sessions accumulate 10-20k tokens appended over 20m.

olivia: Oncall here — immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) route affected customers to smaller model (v11) 2) enable per-session kv limit (soft cap) 3) restart affected worker pods to defragment GPU memory if fragmentation > 3G.

dave: Is there a quick config change we can flip for Dedicated to throttle KV caching? Customers are getting hits on production.

mike: We have a hotfix we can deploy: limit per-session KV entries to 1024 by default and enable periodic KV compaction for sessions that are idle >5m. Also tune allocator to prefer larger contiguous blocks and occasionally do a CUDA IPC-free defrag step on restart.

jasmin: Do we have a safe runtime flag we can toggle without restarting everything? maybe disable aggressive preallocation?

mike: There's a runtime flag `--kv-cache-max-entries` and `--allocator-prealloc` (defaults: off). We can set `--kv-cache-max-entries=1024 --allocator-prealloc=0` for pools and roll config. That avoids restart but will only limit growth; fragmentation likely still present until restart.

tara: Customer-facing: will call customers and route to smaller model while we patch. Anyone able to patch and roll a canary?

jasmin: I can roll a canary to the smallest affected Dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-west-17-3). Plan: update machine config, set kv cap, lower prealloc, enable compaction on idle. Will monitor p99 and GPU frag.

sre-bot: Pager suppressed for ded-west-17-3 during canary rollout (reason=mitigation, owner=jasmin).

mike: Post-deploy metrics we should watch: GPU free mem, allocator fragmentation (we emit `gpu.frag_bytes`), kv_cache entries, per-session token counts, and p95/p99 latency. Add a short-lived alert: if frag_bytes > 3.5G AND p99 > 1.5s -> auto-evacuate new sessions from the host.

olivia: For longer term: two action items: A) allocator tuning — move to a two-zone allocator where small allocations for KV live in separate arenas to reduce fragmentation. B) KV GC — implement epoch-based compacting that evicts stale prefix blocks under memory pressure.

mike: Agreed. We're already prototyping arena split (small/large). Early bench shows fragmentation dive by ~40% under heavy KV growth. But needs careful testing for perf regressions.

dave: Can we also expose a customer configuration to limit retained history? They might prefer app-level control if we enforce defaults.

tara: I've drafted outbound messaging: explain temporary routing to v11 and offer help implementing history pruning. Will send copy after we confirm canary results.

jasmin: Canary update: rolled config at 10:28Z -> `--kv-cache-max-entries=1024 --allocator-prealloc=0 --kv-compact-idle-seconds=300` on ded-west-17-3 (1 pod to start). Observed immediate KV growth rate drop to ~1.4/s and frag_bytes plateaued. p99 dropped from ~2.3s -> 0.9s over 7m.

mike: Nice. Any crash or OOMs during the roll?

jasmin: No new OOMs. We did one pod restart (manual) to reclaim fragmentation and that was the big win.

olivia: Proceed to roll to remaining three pods in pool if no regressions. Keep canary window 20m.

sre-bot: Deploy started: rollout of runtime-config to ded-west-17-3 (3 pods) by jasmin at 10:40Z.

mike: Followups for infra/eng: 
- Add an emergency evict API to drop KV caches for a specific session id (controlled, auditable).
- Add metric `kv.entries_per_session` and make it available in Console per-customer.
- Implement allocator arena split and run extended perf tests.

jasmin: Logged tasks: ENG-5461 (kv-compact), ENG-5462 (allocator-arena-split), ENG-5463 (evict-api). Priorities: ENG-5461 high.

dave: Customer update sent. They accepted routing to v11 and appreciate fast triage.

mike: TL;DR for postmortem: root cause = uncontrolled KV growth from long chat histories + GPU allocator fragmentation -> transient cudaMalloc fails -> CPU page faults -> p99 spike. Mitigations: kv cap + compaction + targeted restarts + allocator tuning. Longer term: arena split + evict API + per-customer visibility.

tara: Thanks team. I'll keep thread active while we finish rollout and collect 1h of stable p99 metrics before closing escalations. :thumbsup:

olivia: Oncall signing off after monitoring window begins. Ping if anything spikes.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed successfully to ded-west-17-3. No failed replicas.

mike: Great work. After metrics stable, let's prep a short postmortem doc with timeline and recommended config defaults for Dedicated.

tara: Will draft postmortem and link here.

(END)
